clue.text: Scoff when a winger appears

definitions.meaning: to scoff is to eat greedily, to gulp food down
a winger here is a bird, something that flies on wings, such as a fork-tailed summer migrant

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the moment a football winger runs onto the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer playing out wide, but it is just a creature with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: gulping food down, and the familiar fork-tailed migrant bird.

clue.text: So crude-may be cleaned up

indicators.note: may be says the letters could become a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Something so filthy might yet be scrubbed clean.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to scrub thoroughly, so something scoured has been cleaned.

clue.text: An entertainer with little heart is testy

indicators.note: with little says only a small part of the following words, the run inside them, is wanted

explanation.surface: A performer with a small heart is irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional performer such as a singer or dancer is an entertainer.

clue.text: Walker takes almost everything allowable

parts.note: a leg is what one walks with

indicators.note: almost says the final letter of the word for everything is dropped

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A hiker grabs nearly all the permitted kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last L of ALL to give AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Permitted by law, so allowable.

clue.text: Get a girl to come round say for a drink

indicators.note: to come round says the girl comes round after the abbreviation for say in the answer

parts.note: to win something is to get it
EG, for example, means say
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Inviting a girlfriend over for a glass of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemmed glass is a vessel used for drinking wine.

clue.text: Stops to take a pull on drink

parts.note: to draw on a pipe or cigarette is to take a pull on it
to sup is to drink, especially in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone pauses to take a swig from their glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that halts comes to a stop at the kerb, an everyday phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Medico behind a military body

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, a medico
aft means behind, at the stern

explanation.surface: A doctor follows a regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment of soldiers sent off for a special duty is a military body.

clue.text: A dunderhead guy splits supporters

annotationWithheld.why: A dunderhead guy splits supporters (9) for ADHERENTS: parse is A + D + HE + RENTS, but D is the head of 'dunder' inside the one word 'dunderhead', so that word is both fodder and indicator

clue.text: A plug for the jumble-sale worker

indicators.note: jumble means mix up, so the letters of sale are shuffled

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone helping at a jumble sale, a charity sale of second-hand goods, gets a plug.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods; here 'jumble' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that seals a gap is a plug, a filler substance.

clue.text: US sportsman's jug

definitions.meaning: a baseball player who throws to the batter; the 's reads as is
a large jug for pouring water

explanation.surface: An American athlete's water jug.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the baseball thrower and a large pouring jug.

clue.text: Figure the top man should be wearing a label

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding, the top man of a military unit
a tag is a label
if you are wearing something you have it on

explanation.surface: An instruction that the boss ought to sport a name badge.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Basically it's a confounded threat

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sums up that, at root, this is a damned threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confounded' reads as a mild oath on the threat, but it is the anagram signal for A THREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describing someone's real nature underneath means fundamentally, an adverb like the definition.

clue.text: Make haste to kindle a candle!

parts.note: to make haste is to rush
to kindle a fire is to light it

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to get a candle lit quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: A rushlight is an old cheap candle made by dipping the pith of a rush in tallow.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned cheap taper made from a rush dipped in fat, so a kind of candle.

clue.text: Bill, taken in by a woman, turned over pass

indicators.note: taken in by says the bill goes inside the woman
turned over says the word for a woman is written backwards

parts.note: her stands for a woman
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A woman takes in a bill and turns it over before passing it along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' applies only to the woman, so the bill sits inside a backwards word; 'pass' means hand over.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass someone the salt is to hand it over to them by stretching out, as in 'can you get me that'.

clue.text: Charges outside left, and fights result

indicators.note: outside means the charges are placed around the letter for left

parts.note: dues are charges or fees

explanation.surface: Fees paid outside the left wing lead to fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal one-to-one fights with pistols or swords, a plural noun like the definition.

clue.text: Understands flying-it's going up and coming down

definitions.text: it's going up and coming down

parts.note: sees means understands, as in I see
awing means on the wing, flying

explanation.surface: Someone realises a bird in flight goes up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving alternately up and down like a playground plank is going up and coming down.

clue.text: A vote for church carpeting

parts.note: X is the cross marked on a ballot paper as a vote
a minster is a large church, such as York Minster

explanation.surface: Someone votes in favour of carpeting the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Axminster is a Devon town that gives its name to a type of woven carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Woven pile carpet named after a Devon town, so a type of carpeting.

clue.text: Many injuries on the pitch can weigh heavily on one

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, so many
ills are harms or injuries
tone is musical pitch

explanation.surface: A footballer's many knocks on the field can be a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a sports field but means musical tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy grinding stone is the image of a burden hung round one's neck.

clue.text: Absurd rules vain general formulated

indicators.note: absurd means ridiculous, so the following letters are made nonsense of and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ridiculous rules drafted by a conceited commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like the conceited military man, but it is the definition, an adjective; 'formulated' adds to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that applies to all cases is general, a direct adjective synonym.

clue.text: Standard dress

definitions.meaning: an official set of clothes worn by members of a group

explanation.surface: Ordinary clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both consistent and the official outfit of a school or force.

clue.text: Inspired attraction in a hostelry

indicators.note: in says the attraction is placed inside the hostelry

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry
a draw is an attraction that pulls in crowds

explanation.surface: Inspired by the appeal of a country pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspired in its literal sense of breathed in, so the air is drawn inwards.

clue.text: Suffer to be well, groomed

definitions.meaning: to suffer a sharp stinging pain
neatly turned out and well-groomed in appearance

explanation.surface: To be in pain is apparently to be healthy and neat.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits 'well' from 'groomed' in the surface, but the two words together give the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to sting with pain and to be neatly and stylishly dressed.

clue.text: A fall from grace in the Orient would be stupid

parts.note: a sin is a fall from grace
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A moral lapse in the East would be foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or foolish in the manner of an ass, so stupid.

clue.text: The youngster keeping close after dark

indicators.note: keeping says the youngster holds the word for close inside

parts.note: a tot is a small child
nigh means near or close

explanation.surface: The child stays near once night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening, during the coming night, so after dark.

clue.text: This country's popular benefit in retirement

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: in retirement means going backwards, so the word for benefit is reversed

parts.note: aid is help, a benefit

explanation.surface: A nation's welfare benefit is well liked by pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: A large country in South Asia; 'This country's' reads as this country is.

clue.text: A Spaniard caught by crooked Italians

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spaniard is caught out by dishonest Italians.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Castile, the central Spanish region, is a Spaniard.

clue.text: Small child getting a letter and a game

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation of child
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A little one receives a letter and a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game played with kings, queens and pawns.

clue.text: Ernie could be the making of her!

indicators.note: could be the making of says the letters of the man's name can be remade

explanation.surface: Ernie might be the man to make a woman's fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' is a woman whose name the anagram produces; it is a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, so a 'her'.

clue.text: Iridescent ring of glass about

annotationWithheld.why: Iridescent ring of glass about (7) for OPALINE: O (ring) can start it but no reading of 'glass about' gives PALINE; the clue as held looks garbled

clue.text: Initiating a break

definitions.meaning: starting or setting something going, as in starting a meeting
a gap or hole, or a chance to get in

explanation.surface: Starting something by making a gap in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both beginning something and a gap or opportunity.

clue.text: Giving a fellow plenty of time to make runs

parts.note: a man is a fellow
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Giving a batsman lots of time to score runs in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture misleads: 'runs' is the verb meaning controls or is in charge of.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business is to manage it, a present-tense verb synonym.

clue.text: Peak the day before others

parts.note: the eve is the day before a festival
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Climbers reach the summit a day ahead of the rest of the party.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest mountain in the world is a peak in the Himalayas.
